classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the vertical tower against the inclined ground to obtain an obtuse interior angle, then find the remaining angle and apply the sine rule.

content.prompt: A vertical tower $AB$ is located on a hill that is inclined at $15^\circ$. From point $C$, 85 metres downhill from the base $A$ of the tower, $\angle BCA$ is measured and found to be $25^\circ$. Find the height $h$ of the tower, correct to the nearest metre.

spec.description: Editable triangle with C downhill from A, vertical AB, horizontal reference through C, and separate 15-degree hill and 25-degree sight-line angle marks. Decorative sky, ground and tower silhouette are omitted.
spec.mathematics: CA = 85 m; CA rises 15 degrees above horizontal; AB is vertical; angle BCA = 25 degrees; AB = h. Coordinates derive from these relationships.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; derived angles and the height are reserved for answers.

inlines.text: Find the remaining angles, then use the sine rule.

answer.worked: Since the tower is vertical, $$\begin{align*}\angle BAC &= 90^\circ+15^\circ\\\angle BAC &= 105^\circ\\\angle ABC &= 180^\circ-105^\circ-25^\circ\\\angle ABC &= 50^\circ.\end{align*}$$ By the sine rule, $$\begin{align*}\frac{h}{\sin25^\circ} &= \frac{85}{\sin50^\circ}\\h &= \frac{85\sin25^\circ}{\sin50^\circ}\\h &\approx 47\,\mathrm{m}.\end{align*}$$
